subject: Everleaf pilot: tier switchability & feature bundle constraints
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@everleafhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ryu <tryu@everleafhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot procurement question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — a couple of quick practical questions before we lock the pilot:

1) If we start on the Compact tier for the 3-month pilot and need to switch to the Core tier mid-pilot because usage spikes, what’s the process and lead time? Will we get prorated credits back if we step down later?

2) We plan to enable the NER and Reranking add-ons for a small subset of flows. Can those be bundled to a pilot-only feature set (i.e., not on the seat count for the org-wide license) and then rolled into the main contract later?

We’ve got a procurement review on Friday; appreciate a short note so we can surface options.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Procurement Manager — Everleaf Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@everleafhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot procurement question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up top, details below.

TL;DR:
- Upgrades (Compact -> Core) are effective immediately; we allow same-day capacity changes with billing prorated to the day.
- Downgrades inside the contracted pilot window are allowed but subject to a 30-day notice for a full credit reconciliation; we provide pro-rated credits for unused committed capacity, applied to future invoices or convertible to usage credits for 90 days.
- Pilot-only add-ons (NER, Reranking) can be enabled as "feature seats" for the pilot cohort; we can map them to entitlements that either disappear after pilot or convert to org-wide entitlements at renewal with an agreed transition discount.

I’ve attached a simple pricing matrix and a short MAAP (mutual action plan) showing timing/credits. If you want, Ben (cc’d) can run a quick scenario showing cost delta for a mid-pilot 2x usage spike.

Next steps: I can send a concise amendment template that covers upgrade/downgrade windows and feature entitlements, or we can sign the pilot as-is and add an addendum. Which do you prefer for Friday?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot procurement question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Ben / Kim — quick internal: Alicia wants clear language for upgrade immediate, downgrade 30-day notice + prorated credits. She specifically asked that the pilot-only add-ons not be treated as permanent seat entitlements unless they convert at renewal with a transition discount.

Can you sketch two options we can present Friday:
- Option A: Flexible pilot amendment (no upfront commit, pay-as-you-go with on-demand upgrade to Core; downgrade credits limited to usage credits)
- Option B: Small committed pilot (3-month Compact commit with 20% discount, allows 1 mid-pilot free upgrade to Core; downgrade allowed but credits reconcilation 30 days after change)

If we include the MAAP addendum we can mitigate procurement risk. Ben — would a 10% transition discount on add-ons at renewal be reasonable?

Thanks,
—Sean

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot procurement question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Quick take:
- Present both options. Procurement teams like the certainty of Option B but with one free mid-pilot upgrade baked in.
- For Step-down credits: offer prorated invoice credit for committed GPU-hours or token-commit that are unconsumed; if they prefer immediate cash credit, we can offer usage-credit-only (non-cash).
- Add-ons: offer pilot entitlements scoped to a team alias (e.g. everleaf-pilot@everleafhealth.com). If they convert at renewal, apply a 10% one-time conversion discount for the first 12 months of the full contract.

I’ll draft stipend language and the amendment clause (30-day notice for downgrade with automated credit calc). Kim, can you check whether this needs legal sign-off or we can do via scope amendment?

—Ben

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@everleafhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot amendment options + MAAP (attached)

Hi Alicia — attaching the pricing matrix and a short MAAP as promised. Two clean options below that you can surface in Friday’s review.

Option A — Flex pilot (no commit)
• Billing: pay-as-you-go at Compact rates.
• Upgrade: immediate to Core; billed pro-rata from upgrade day.
• Downgrade: allowed; credits issued as usage credit only, valid 90 days.
• Add-ons: enabled for pilot alias; do not count towards org seats. No conversion unless agreed at renewal.

Option B — Committed pilot (3 months)
• Billing: 3-month Compact commit (20% off list).
• Upgrade: one complimentary mid-pilot upgrade to Core (no extra commit), subsequent upgrades bill pro-rata.
• Downgrade: 30-day notice required; unused committed capacity reconciled and issued as invoice credit (non-cash) or usage credit by election.
• Add-ons: pilot entitlements scoped to the pilot alias; conversion to org entitlements at renewal with 10% conversion discount for 12 months.

I’ve linked the MAAP and included a one-page amendment template that we can sign electronically. If you want Ben to show cost examples for a 2x usage spike, we can run that immediately.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix-everleaf.xlsx (xlsx), Everleaf-MAAP_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — if you prefer, I can convert Option B into an agreement with the specific language procurement wants and route for signature before your Friday review.

Best,
Sean

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@everleafhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ryu <tryu@everleafhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 18:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot amendment options + MAAP (attached)

Thanks Sean — this is exactly what we needed. Two quick clarifying asks before I present:

1) For Option B, can you make the downgrade credit explicitly convertible to a HubSpot invoice credit line? Our finance team prefers invoice-level credits over usage coupons.
2) For add-ons, would the pilot alias approach block us from enabling add-ons for a second pilot cohort if we expand? If so, what’s the cost to extend pilot entitlements to an additional 5 pilot users?

If you can answer those two in a short bullet list I’ll include with procurement. If we can get the amendment in DocuSign today we’ll move forward.

Appreciate it,
Alicia
Procurement Manager — Everleaf Health
